case_name: Krishnamoorthy & Anr v State By Inspector Of Police & Ors
facts: The deceased Dhanabagyam went to her groundnut field on October 5, 1996.
Mahadevan (PW-2) heard some noise and saw A-1 (Vijayan) running from the field.
Suresh Kumar (PW-1), son of the deceased, found his mother's body with head injuries and missing jewels.
A-3 surrendered and made an extra judicial confession that he and other accused robbed Dhanabagyam and killed her.
The police recovered stones used in the offence and identified A-1, A-2, A-3, and A-4 as the accused.
issues: Whether the prosecution has established a chain of circumstances leading to an inescapable conclusion that the accused committed the crime.
Whether the confessions made by the accused are reliable evidence.
petitioner_arguments: There is no direct evidence to connect them with the incident and the offence.
The question of PW-2 identifying all four accused did not arise, as he only saw A-1 running away from the field.
court_reasoning: The trial court and High Court held that the evidence shows a complete unbroken chain of circumstances unerringly leading to an inescapable conclusion that the accused had committed the crime.

Though the confessions made to Police are to be excluded, when examined with reference to the other proved circumstances, and the recoveries made on the information furnished by the accused, the guilt of the accused stood established.
holding: The Supreme Court affirmed the decision of the trial court and High Court, holding that the prosecution had established a chain of circumstances leading to an inescapable conclusion that the accused committed the crime.
